name: Zabad
overview: Zabad is a male figure mentioned in the book of Ezra as a descendant of Zattu. He is noted particularly for having married a foreign wife, a detail that highlights issues addressed during the post-exilic period regarding intermarriage. No tribal affiliation or additional personal notes are recorded for him.
namesAndTitles: The name Zabad means 'he bestows,' which is a proper name of Hebrew origin. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it reflects a common theophoric naming pattern in the Old Testament.
familyAndRelationships: Zabad is explicitly identified as a descendant of Zattu, establishing a direct familial link. Beyond this, Scripture does not record any further family relationships for him apart from his marriage to a foreign wife.
scriptureSignificance: Zabad's significance lies in his representation of the challenges faced by the Israelites returning from exile, particularly concerning the issue of intermarriage with foreign women. His mention in Ezra 10:27 serves as a testament to the community's efforts to maintain covenantal purity in obedience to God's commands. This highlights the broader biblical theme of faithfulness to God's covenant amidst cultural pressures.
